question: What is the work done in moving a charge of 10 C between two points with a potential difference of 14 V?
solution:
The correct answer is __**140 J**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Work Done Formula:** The work done in moving a charge between two points is calculated using the formula: *Work Done (W) = Charge (Q) × Potential Difference (V)*.
 
• In this case, the **charge (Q)** is **10 C**, and the **potential difference (V)** is **14 V**.
 
• Substituting the values: *W = 10 × 14 = 140 J.* Hence, the work done is **140 J**. *This calculation is correct.*
 
• ** The unit of work done is Joules (J**), which is derived as: *1 Joule = 1 Coulomb × 1 Volt.* This confirms the calculation.
 
• Moving a charge in an electric field involves work done proportional to the potential difference and the magnitude of the charge. *Hence, 140 J is the correct value.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Electric Potential and Work:**

 
 
• **Electric potential** is the work done per unit charge to move a charge from one point to another in an electric field.
 
• The **potential difference** between two points in an electric field represents the amount of work required to move a unit charge between those points.
 
• Work is directly proportional to both the **charge (Q)** and the **potential difference (V)**.
 
 
 
• **Application of Work Done:**
 
 
• This principle is used in various applications, such as **batteries, capacitors, and electric circuits**, where energy transfer occurs due to movement of charges.
 
• In physics, work done in moving charges is fundamental to studying **electric fields**, **potential energy**, and **circuit behavior**.
 
 
 
• **Units and Measurement:**
 
 
• The unit of work is **Joule**, and the unit of potential difference is **Volt** (V).
 
• Charge is measured in **Coulombs**, denoted by the symbol **C**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Key Concepts in Electric Work:**

 
 
• **Potential difference:** This is a measure of the difference in electric potential between two points, and it drives the movement of charges in an electric field.
 
• **Work done:** It is an essential concept in energy transfer and the study of circuits, as it determines the energy required to perform electrical operations.
 
 
 
• **Applications:**
 
 
• The principle of work done is applied in **electric motors, generators, and energy storage devices**, which rely on the movement of charges.
 
• It is also fundamental in understanding the functioning of **batteries** and **electrical appliances**.
